title: Reserving a big array
description:
Reserve address space for a huge array and commit pages only as it grows.

```
reserved 1 GB of addresses, committed 0
push 1,000 items -> committed 1 page (4 KB)
push 1,000,000 items -> committed 977 pages
no copies ever made (the array never moves)
```
hints: The bytes needed after a push are `m_size * sizeof(int)`; the pages needed are that rounded up to 4096 (lesson 6.03).
Because the addresses are reserved up front, pointers to items stay valid forever, unlike `std::vector`.
requirements: Model it with page states (reserved / committed), or on Windows use `VirtualAlloc` with `MEM_RESERVE` and then `MEM_COMMIT`.
Commit the next page only when a push crosses into it.
stretch: Do it for real on Windows and watch the process's commit size in Task Manager.
